verses.mystical_translation: An altar of measured proportions — an enacted threshold where proportion and offering meet.
The cast sea — a bounded circle of water and metal, holding an inner order.
Bovine forms bear the bowl — layered strength arrayed beneath the water-holder.
Four directions upheld by twelve guardians whose faces mark compass points; their inward rears turn the outside away.
A thin rim, flowered like a chalice; inside, a vast capacity beyond the human hand.
Arrayed basins shape ritual movement; some cleanse the offerings, the greater basin serves the officiants.
Light multiplied symmetrically—gold stands set like constellations flanking the sacred center.
Tables line the halls, vessels of gold multiply — abundance for sustenance and service.
Thresholds are made of earth and metal; coverings of common metal mark access to solemn spaces.
The great basin sits at the temple’s eastern flank, facing the southern approach.
A craftsman completes his appointed pieces — a named hand that shapes the temple’s tools.
Columns crowned with embossed wreaths: erected signs that mark the threshold of presence.
Fruit repeated in rows—pomegranate rotas as a patterned veil over the column crowns.
Underpinnings and their bowls: support fashioned to hold ritual action.
One vessel borne by a dozen beasts — unity upheld by a structure of service.
A line of makers across generations furnishes the house of presence with burnished service.
Where soil holds water, metal took form — in the plain the casting gathered communal labor.
Abundance so great that measure fails — weight beyond accounting becomes a witness to overflow.
Every table and altar fashioned — places for offerings and for the bread that stands before presence.
Burnished lights placed before the oracle — rule and splendour in gold.
Floral motifs, tools, and fire-holders, all rendered in the same bright metal that signals offering.
Tools of tending and thresholds alike are gilded — the making of access and maintenance into a luminous act.

contemplative_note: The chapter centers craft and abundance: human skill shaping common metals into vessels intended to mediate the holy.
